# Qu

> An array language for measurement science: signals, spectra, impedance,
> and the figures that go in the paper. Interpreted, with a numerical
> standard library and a publication-quality plotting backend that exports
> PDF with embedded fonts, SVG and TikZ.

Qu ships an MCP server, so an assistant does not have to guess at all:
`qu mcp` speaks JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout and exposes six tools —
`qu_eval` runs source and returns what it printed, `qu_check` parses without
executing, `qu_builtins` answers from the interpreter's own dispatch table,
`qu_docs` reads a page, `qu_figure` returns the figure a script draws as SVG,
and `qu_run_file` runs a file. Calls are sandboxed and time-limited. Add it
with `claude mcp add qu -- qu mcp`, or the equivalent `mcpServers` block in
any MCP client.

Failing that, an assistant that has read the two files below can write
correct Qu without guessing. Read `llms-agent-guide.md` first — it is short,
and it is mostly about the places where Qu differs from the language you
would otherwise assume.

## Essential

- [Agent guide](docs/llms-agent-guide.md): the differences that cause wrong
  code — evaluation rules, argument orders, and the traps, each with the
  error message it produces.
- [Builtin index](book/src/stdlib/builtin-index.md): every function name the
  engine answers to, generated from the interpreter's own table. If a name
  is not here, the engine does not have it.

## Language

- [Specification](docs/qu-language-spec.md): normative, and ahead of the
  engine in places — treat the builtin index as the authority on what
  exists.
- [From Zero](book/src/getting-started/from-zero.md): a complete first
  session that runs as written, no external data.
- [Fundamentals](book/src/getting-started/book1-fundamentals.md): types,
  contracts, control flow, error handling.

## Standard library
